page: Vultr vbm-6c-32gb is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 2286G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via hyperthreading, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a bundled 1920 GB local SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates balanced processing capabilities, with average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests. The server demonstrates strong single-threaded compression and decompression speeds, reaching 35.51 GB/sec in gzip and 13.91 GB/sec in bzip3. However, a notable performance tradeoff exists in memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks, where read and write speeds fall into the lower tier. Conversely, the Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, indicating highly efficient cached memory operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers dedicated, non-virtualized hardware resources and a substantial local SSD storage allocation, making it a viable option for workloads requiring consistent physical resource access without hypervisor overhead. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis caching, and moderate database operations. It is less optimal for memory-intensive uncached processing or larger LLM inference tasks, as demonstrated by weak performance on 7B parameter models.
